questions.question_text: Suggest a suitable hypothesis to investigate how the characteristics of a river change downstream (do not choose size of bedload or angle of slope). [1]

keywords_required: The channel width increases with distance downstream. (OR The river velocity increases downstream, OR The river depth increases downstream).

questions.question_text: Identify two advantages of doing a pilot study before beginning the main fieldwork. [2]

keywords_required: To practise the fieldwork techniques and ensure equipment works correctly.
To identify any potential safety hazards or flaws in the methodology before the real data collection.

questions.question_text: Devise three suitable questions that students could use in a questionnaire to find out how successful the regeneration of a town centre has been. [3]

keywords_required: 1. On a scale of 1-10, how satisfied are you with the new town centre?
2. Do you feel the new pedestrian zones have improved shopping access?
3. Has the regeneration improved the visual appearance of the town?

questions.question_text: Why is sampling a useful fieldwork technique? [2]

keywords_required: It saves time and money, as it is impossible to measure every single item (e.g. every pebble) or ask every single person.
If done correctly (random or systematic), it provides a representative subset of data that reflects the whole population.

questions.question_text: Suggest how students could make sure that their bi-polar survey results are reliable. [2]

keywords_required: Have multiple students score the same site independently and then calculate an average score to reduce subjectivity/bias.
Conduct the survey at the same time of day at all sites so conditions (like traffic noise) are comparable.
